cards.lead: Human origins in Africa established from fossils
cards.name: Human origins in Africa from fossils (Taung, Sterkfontein, Olduvai)
cards.summary: Fossil finds in South Africa and Tanzania showed that upright walking hominins with small brains preceded large-brained humans and that the human lineage arose in Africa.
cards.description: Raymond Dart published the Taung child skull in Nature in 1925 as an extinct ape intermediate between living anthropoids and man. Fossils found at Sterkfontein from 1936 and at Olduvai Gorge in 1959 and 1964 extended the record, and Leakey, Tobias and Napier named Homo habilis from Olduvai in 1964. The sources support the African lineage through these finds, but Dart's claim was largely dismissed at first.
cards.origin_note: Dart's 1925 Taung paper is the first published fossil claim in these sources for an African ape-man intermediate between apes and man; the sources cite no earlier one.

impact.note: Scores kept from the lead: the finds reshaped the account of human origins for the science community, and later fossil work rested on them.

cards.lead: Chromosome theory of heredity and gene mapping in New York
cards.note: Sutton (Columbia) and Boveri (Munich) proposed the chromosome theory in 1902-1903, so the 1902 date and the claim of first_known for the theory belong to them. The sources do not show whether Morgan's group derived the theory from Sutton, so origin is unknown; the card covers the New York gene-mapping line from 1910 to 1913.
cards.name: Chromosome theory and gene mapping in the Morgan lab (New York)
cards.summary: Sutton and Boveri linked Mendel's factors to chromosomes, and Morgan's group then located genes on chromosomes and drew the first genetic map.
cards.description: Walter Sutton, at Columbia, and Theodor Boveri, in Munich, independently argued that chromosomes carry heredity. Thomas Hunt Morgan's Drosophila work at Columbia from 1910 tied a white-eye trait to the sex chromosome, and Alfred Sturtevant's 1913 map put six sex-linked genes in linear order. The sources support these steps, but not a direct line of derivation from Sutton to Morgan.
cards.origin_note: Sutton and Boveri reached similar conclusions independently, but the sources do not say whether Morgan's group knew of Sutton's work when it began.

impact.note: Scores kept from the lead: the gene map and chromosome linkage became the base for much later Drosophila and mammalian genetics.

cards.name: Deciphering the genetic code (poly-U, triplet proof, full codon table)
cards.summary: Nirenberg, Matthaei, Crick and Brenner showed that the genetic code is read as triplets, and Nirenberg's group assigned the 64 codons by 1966.
cards.description: Marshall Nirenberg and Heinrich Matthaei showed in 1961 that a synthetic uracil-only RNA directed the synthesis of phenylalanine in cell-free E. coli. Crick, Barnett, Brenner and Watts-Tobin proved in Nature in December 1961 that the code is a triplet code, and Nirenberg announced the sixty-four codon assignments by 1966. The 1968 Nobel Prize was shared by Nirenberg, Holley and Khorana.
cards.origin_note: The sources describe the poly-U experiment as the first step in deciphering the code and cite no earlier codon assignment.

impact.note: Scores kept from the lead: reading the code changed how biology understood heredity and made protein engineering possible.

cards.name: Programmable genome editing with CRISPR-Cas9
cards.summary: Guide RNAs were shown in 2012 to program Cas9 to cut chosen DNA, and by 2013 Cas9 was used to edit several sites in mammalian cells.
cards.description: Jinek and colleagues showed in Science in 2012 that a crRNA with a trans-activating crRNA guides Cas9 to cut target DNA, and that engineered RNA could program the cut. Cong, Ran, Zhang and colleagues reported in 2013 that Cas9 with short RNAs cut endogenous loci in human and mouse cells, and that several guides could edit several sites at once.
cards.origin_note: The sources present the 2012 papers as the first demonstration of guide-RNA programming of Cas9; the CRISPR repeats are background only and are not claimed as the editing capability.

impact.note: Scores kept from the lead: cheap gene editing became routine in research and the first editing therapies followed.
